material_findings.title: ETHOnline prize surface expands to 11 sponsor pools totaling $79,000

The Graph still includes a $5,000 Continuity AI Tooling / AI Use Case track that can extend an existing open-source project under event-specific provenance rules. ETHGlobal's global rules confirm that participants stake cryptocurrency to confirm a spot and can recover the hackathon stake by meeting minimum participation/submission requirements.

material_findings.title: Liezz introduces adversarial witness injection for ZK DSL toolchain testing
material_findings.summary: arXiv:2608.30648 describes Liezz, a framework that generates deterministic ZK DSL programs and injects adversarially spliced witnesses. The authors report support for Circom, Corset, Gnark, and Noir and 13 discovered bugs, seven with soundness impact, while a valid-execution baseline did not expose those soundness failures under the same testing budget.
material_findings.recommended_action: Review the full paper and locate any released implementation. Before adoption, verify license, deterministic fixtures, supported compiler versions, reproducibility of reported bugs, and whether its witness-injection model adds reusable local/authorized ZK testing capability rather than duplicating existing tools.

material_findings.title: New algebraic Search-LWE algorithm claims polynomial improvement over prior Groebner approaches
material_findings.summary: arXiv:2608.29977 proposes a Search-LWE algorithm combining linear algebra with S-polynomial/Groebner-basis methods and claims a polynomial complexity improvement over prior Groebner-basis approaches while avoiding semi-regularity assumptions in its complexity analysis. The paper is explicitly under peer review.
material_findings.recommended_action: Do not turn the abstract into a capability claim. Review parameter regimes, asymptotics, implementation availability, and comparisons with lattice/combinatorial solvers before deciding whether it warrants a benchmark fixture or solver research note.

material_findings.title: RsaWebTool is a broad browser RSA/CTF candidate with an external-reporting side effect
material_findings.summary: The public non-archived yuzu-octopus/RsaWebTool README describes 47 RSA attacks plus RSA/AES/ECC/hash/DH calculators, browser-side BigInt checks and SageMathCell fallback. It also documents automatic submission of discovered factorizations to FactorDB. Latest visible commits in this pass are from July 26, 2026, and a root LICENSE file or explicit repository license was not verified.
material_findings.recommended_action: Do not import yet. First verify licensing and dependencies, disable FactorDB reporting/external calls, reproduce a small representative attack set on deterministic local CTF fixtures, and compare overlap with RsaCracker/RsaCtfTool and existing suite capabilities.
